title: Prefs/Extcap: Added support for password which is never stored on the disk
description:
Issue:
When a user sets extcap password, it is not remembered during runtime.
Therefore when the user runs extcap twice in row, password must be
entered over and over.

Solution:
New prefs type PREF_PASSWORD defined and extcap framework is adapted to
it.
It has welcomed consequence. Because now prefs key exists in prefs,
e.g. tshark can change it with -o option so it can run extcaps which
requires password. It was not possible to run such extcap with tshark
before.

Changes:
- PREF_PASSWORD handled nearly same way as PREF_STRING
  - new API calls added to register/set/get password
  - prefs key and description is stored in prefs file
  - password value is never stored nor read
  - UI editor shows password just during entering new password
    (PasswordEchoOnEdit), dots shown elsewhere
- extcap framework adapted to map EXTCAP_ARG_PASSWORD to PREF_PASSWORD

What would be the easiest way to test this change? Thanks.

My procedure:
1. Query every extcap from cli about config and find all password items (type=password). There are many of them.
2. With nonpatched wireshark run extcap with password and then reopen config dialog - password is empty, because wireshark do not remember passwords between extcap runs
3. With patched wireshark run same as above and passwords are remembered
4. Check prefs config - you will see password entries, but no values
5. Exit and start patched wireshark again - passwords are away in extcap dialogs, but will be remembered between runs

Good extcap candidates are ones which require password to login somewhere - ciscodump, ssh remote capture. !You should use password authentication, not keys!

With nonpatched wireshark every second run will fail because wireshark forgots password. With patched wireshark it works fine till wireshark is exited.
OK thanks. I will try to find time to test it.

Issue:

Changes:

    (PasswordEchoOnEdit), dots shown elsewhere

- updated tools/checkAPIs.pl to allow to ignore some cases in prefs_register_*_preference which are caused by this patch
